subject: shinysky - Confirm alert does not work

messages.author: 352166904028c0ad
messages.subject: shinysky - Confirm alert does not work
parts:
Hi all,

I am working on a app where I want to inform the user about a critical input. In this alert the user should have the option to confirm his input and proceed. I am using shinysky for the alert and I am inserting a button for the confirmation. Unfortunately shiny ignores the pressing of the button completely.

Can anyone help me? I have no clue why that is not working.

My source:

library(shiny)
library(shinysky)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    shinyalert("idTestAlert", auto.close.after = 5),
    actionButton("idTestBtn", "Show Alert"),
    verbatimTextOutput("idText")),
  server = function(session, input, output) {
    btnCounter <- reactive({
      if (is.null(input[["idTest"]])) 0
      else input[["idTest"]]
    })
    observe({
      if (input$idTestBtn>0)
        showshinyalert(session,
                       "idTestAlert",
                       "Test <button id='idTest' type='button' class='btn btn-warning'>Confirm</button>",
                       styleclass="warning")
    })
    output$idText <- renderText({btnCounter()})
  }
)

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: shinysky - Confirm alert does not work
parts:
@Micahel Frank.

I think I have found a (hacky and probably not recommended) solution in ShinySky.

The solution has nothing to do with ShinySky per se but has a lot to do with how Shiny works.

I think when you create a button like that dynamically using pure HTML Shiny actually doesn't know that it exists. From this page of the Shiny tutorial we see that it is recommended that we run shiny.unbindAll(); before we insert a new dynamic component and shiny.bindAll() after. I think bindAll() will run some code that scans the HTML DOM for shiny componenents and makes it available for use. So that's what I have done.

Solution Code

library(shiny)
library(shinysky)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
shinyalert("idTestAlert", auto.close.after = 105, click.hide = F),

actionButton("idTestBtn", "Show Alert"),
    verbatimTextOutput("idText")),
  server = function(session, input, output) {
    btnCounter <- reactive({
browser()

if (is.null(input[["idTest"]])) 0
      else input[["idTest"]]
    })
    observe({
      if (input$idTestBtn>0)        
        showshinyalert(session,
                       "idTestAlert",
HTML("<script>Shiny.unbindAll();  </script>Test <button id='idTest' type='button' class='btn action-button btn-warning'>Confirm</button> <script>Shiny.bindAll();</script>"),

styleclass="warning")
    })
        
    
    output$idText <- renderText({btnCounter()})
  }
)

I think I have found a (hacky and probably not recommended) solution in ShinySky.

The solution has nothing to do with ShinySky per se but has a lot to do with how Shiny works.

I think when you create a button like that dynamically using pure HTML Shiny actually doesn't know that it exists. From this page of the Shiny tutorial we see that it is recommended that we run shiny.unbindAll(); before we insert a new dynamic component and shiny.bindAll() after. library(shiny)
library(shinysky)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    shinyalert("idTestAlert", auto.close.after = 105, click.hide = F),
    actionButton("idTestBtn", "Show Alert"),
    verbatimTextOutput("idText")),
  server = function(session, input, output) {
    btnCounter <- reactive({
      browser()
      if (is.null(input[["idTest"]])) 0
      else input[["idTest"]]
    })
    observe({
      if (input$idTestBtn>0)        
        showshinyalert(session,
                       "idTestAlert", 
                       HTML("<script>Shiny.unbindAll();  </script>Test <button id='idTest' type='button' class='btn action-button btn-warning'>Confirm</button> <script>Shiny.bindAll();</script>"),
                       styleclass="warning")
    })
        
    
    output$idText <- renderText({btnCounter()})
  }
